answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake that vests over time: a new account can harbor no reputation until it has done useful, attested work, so an attacker must fund every fake identity separately. Like a lotus that blooms only after a season underwater, trust grows slowly while cost is paid upfront, and misbehavior burns the stake, pushing the horizon for profitable abuse beyond what cheap mass-created identities can reach.
